items_fixed.description: Core correctness bug: candidates[i].judgment_ledger and lattice_adjudication.ledgers[j] were the SAME object (elect.ts's ledgerById map, built from adjudication.ledgers with no copy), so the new budget-trim sections (minKeep:0, not hardFloor) mutating ledger fields reached THROUGH lattice_adjudication.ledgers[] also silently emptied the surviving candidate's own protected judgment_ledger.dosas_present/.residual_dosas/.pariharas_applied -- exactly the 'densest, most-actionable layer' the candidates section's hardFloor:true exists to protect.
items_fixed.detail: Added cloneJudgmentLedgerForCandidate() (deep-copies all 7 JudgmentLedger array fields: dosas_present, pariharas_applied, residual_dosas, supporting_factors, neutral_annotations, convention_only_factors, convention_only_keys; scalar fields shared via spread since they're immutable primitives) and used it building ledgerById, so each candidate's judgment_ledger is now an independent copy. Chose the deep-copy option (not the alternative hardFloor+minKeep:1 option) because it preserves the PR's existing tiered trim design (A-G stay disposable bookkeeping copies of the SAME logical data, candidates stays the sole protected hardFloor tier) with a minimal, surgical change. Wrote a new dedicated regression test, elect_ledger_alias_f122.test.ts, that builds a 2-candidate response with real dosha/residual/parihara content (25/20/5), tunes budget_kb to force a trim of lattice_adjudication.ledgers[]'s bookkeeping arrays while both candidates survive, and asserts both survivors' own judgment_ledger array counts are still intact (not just reduced) PLUS a direct object-identity check (candidate.judgment_ledger !== the corresponding lattice_adjudication.ledgers[] entry). Verified genuinely: temporarily reverted the clone (reinstating the alias) via Edit (never git stash, per instructions), re-ran the test -- it failed cleanly on the exact symptom (dosas_present came back 12/0 instead of 25/25 for the two 'surviving' candidates, even though neither candidate was removed by the hardFloor mechanism), then restored the fix and re-confirmed green.

items_fixed.description: New dangling references after trim: pareto.frontier_candidate_ids/dominated_candidate_ids were not synced to the surviving candidate set after the candidates section trims lattice_adjudication.ledgers, so a trimmed response could advertise a frontier_candidate_id with no corresponding ledger.
items_fixed.detail: Synced pareto.frontier_candidate_ids and dominated_candidate_ids to the same survivingIds set the existing ledgers-sync already computes, inside the candidates section's setArray. Deliberately left gap_report and density UNSYNCED with an explanatory code comment: both are whole-horizon aggregate statistics computed once over the full pre-trim set (gap_report.statement's 'N of M candidates survive' prose, census_disposition_counts; density's cited/convention row counts) and hold no candidate_id that could dangle the way frontier/dominated_candidate_ids could -- rewriting them post-trim would make them describe the served response rather than the engine's computation, which is the opposite of what a gap report is for. An independent code-reviewer agent verified this reasoning is factually correct (LatticeGapReport and the density type genuinely contain no candidate_id fields) and that the sync has no null/undefined crash paths (ParetoResult's two arrays are non-optional string[], the whole block stays guarded by the pre-existing `if (c.lattice_adjudication)` check).

items_fixed.description: Two hollow verification signals: ekv_controls.py::_check_f122 was a whole-file substring grep (would PASS even if the real TrimmableSection were deleted, as long as a matching string survived elsewhere in the file, e.g. a comment); neither new PR test file was on CI's platform-mcp allowlist in .github/workflows/ci.yml, so 'N/N passing' was local-only.
items_fixed.detail: ekv_controls.py fixed in TWO passes. First pass confined matching to buildElectSections()'s own function body and required each path to appear as a `path: '...'` key followed by getArray:/setArray: within an 800-char lookahead window. An independent code-reviewer agent then found this first fix still had a real blind spot: measured the actual spacing between consecutive path: declarations in the real file (648-786 chars) -- smaller than the 800-char window -- so the window reliably bled into the NEXT section's getArray:/setArray: text, and a genuine regression (one section's getArray/setArray deleted, path/label/minKeep/recover left intact) still false-PASSed for 6 of the 7 required paths. Second pass replaced the fixed window with _find_top_level_object_spans(), a comment- and string-aware brace-matching parser that correctly bounds each TrimmableSection's own object literal (skips // line comments, /* */ block comments, and quoted-string contents before counting braces, so an apostrophe inside a comment like "caller's own real source" can't desync the brace count). Verified: (a) PASSes on the real, correct elect.ts; (b) reproduced the reviewer's exact getArray/setArray-deletion regression via a scripted mutation (never edited the tracked file directly) and confirmed the new detector correctly FAILs with 'no getArray/setArray within its own section object'; (c) confirmed the original file was left untouched (diff stat unchanged) after the mutation test. Also added elect_budget_trim_f122.test.ts, elect_sections_coverage.test.ts, and the new elect_ledger_alias_f122.test.ts to the CI allowlist step in .github/workflows/ci.yml (validated YAML syntax with python's yaml.safe_load and confirmed all three referenced paths exist on disk).
items_fixed.verification_note: Item 3's fix itself went through one round of independent review that caught a real gap in my first attempt (the 800-char window) -- documented here rather than silently corrected, per the campaign's earned-signal doctrine (CLAUDE.md SS N.8): a detector that could still be fooled is not the same claim as a detector that can't.

items_fixed.description: Misleading comment in elect.ts claiming 'sections are in density order (lowest-density first)' when the trimmer actually re-sorts by byte size within a hardFloor tier, not by declaration order.
items_fixed.detail: Corrected the buildElectSections() doc-comment to explain what response_budget.ts::applyResponseBudget actually does: splits sections into two TIERS by hardFloor (non-hardFloor first, hardFloor last), and WITHIN each tier sorts by each section's own current serialized byte size, biggest-first -- not declaration order. Clarified that the real invariant the file's declaration order enforces is the TIER split (A-G + convention_only_factors are all non-hardFloor, so they're always exhausted before candidates is ever touched), not which of A-G gets cut first.
